established_findings.statement: LLMs are actively researched and applied to NetOps tasks including intent-driven configuration translation, fault diagnosis/AIOps, intent assurance, and multi-agent network management frameworks.
limitations: Many sources are surveys, system descriptions, or single-organization reports rather than large-scale controlled deployments
Domain specialization (telecom, datacenter, IoT) limits generality across all NetOps settings

established_findings.statement: Hallucination, factual errors, and unreliable outputs from LLMs are central reliability concerns for operational NetOps use-cases; active detection and mitigation research addresses these risks.
limitations: Detection/mitigation approaches are heterogeneous and evaluated under differing conditions
Few studies report end-to-end operational outcomes specifically for NetOps workflows

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented and agentic LLM architectures (LLMs invoking verifiers, simulators, or domain tools) are proposed and empirically evaluated as a strategy to improve reliability and functionality for operational tasks.
limitations: Evaluations vary in scale and task realism
Effectiveness depends on the quality and integration of external tools

established_findings.statement: Deterministic/formal network configuration verification tools and scalable verifiers (e.g., distributed Batfish-based verifiers) exist and can validate network properties at large scale.
limitations: Applicability depends on the modeled properties (reachability, control-plane simulation) and required abstractions
Distributed verification can incur substantial resource and time costs for very large networks

established_findings.statement: Prompt injection and adversarial prompting are recognized threats to LLM pipelines; practical detection and mitigation frameworks have been proposed and evaluated.
limitations: Evaluations use specific attack corpora; transferability to NetOps-formatted adversarial inputs is not uniformly validated
Operational integration and latency trade-offs are not consistently reported

established_findings.statement: Methodological work emphasizes the need for standardized evaluation practices for RAG/tool-augmented LLM systems and NetOps-specific benchmarks; several papers propose blueprints or domain-specific benchmarks.
limitations: Proposed benchmarks and blueprints are early-stage and domain-specific; no universally accepted NetOps benchmark is established in the supplied records
Different operational properties require distinct validators and metrics

unresolved_questions.statement: To what degree can LLM-generated network configurations or NetOps actions be executed autonomously in production without unacceptable operational risk?
limitations: Production reports (e.g., Confucius) describe onboarded applications but do not constitute broad multi-vendor validation
Surveys highlight risks but lack quantitative deployment-failure rates

unresolved_questions.statement: Can LLMs reliably self-correct NetOps-specific errors without external deterministic verification signals?
limitations: Evidence indicates self-correction rarely succeeds absent reliable external feedback/oracles; NetOps-specific experiments are limited
Success is task-dependent; tasks with reliable external oracles fare better

unresolved_questions.statement: What standardized datasets and metrics best represent operational correctness (safety, policy compliance, reachability) for evaluating LLM-driven NetOps pipelines?
limitations: Multiple proposals exist but consensus and large-scale public corpora for realistic configs are not established in the supplied records
Different operational properties require distinct validators and metrics

candidate_gaps.statement: Systematic empirical evaluations comparing end-to-end generate–validate–repair pipelines (LLM generation + formal verifier + repair loop) against human or traditional automation baselines for NetOps tasks are limited.
limitations: Some frameworks integrate validation (e.g., Confucius) but comparative, reproducible trials at scale are not reported in the supplied records
Variation in task definitions and validators complicates direct comparison

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirically validated adversarial-robustness evaluations and defenses tailored to NetOps artifacts (configs, CLI sequences, topology descriptions) are sparse.
limitations: Existing defenses are evaluated on general prompt-injection corpora; direct tests against NetOps-formatted adversarial inputs are not prominent in the supplied records
Operational constraints (latency, tool-call budgets) affect practicability

candidate_gaps.statement: Large, public, realistic corpora of router/device configurations and annotated operational failures for training/evaluating LLMs in NetOps are insufficiently standardized and available.
limitations: Some datasets and topologies are used in verifier papers, but a widely adopted public NetOps-config benchmark is not documented in the supplied records
Data sensitivity and anonymization barriers limit public release

candidate_gaps.statement: Operational cost/latency and tool-orchestration trade-offs (e.g., invoking heavy verifiers or multiple tools per change) require quantification in agentic NetOps pipelines.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: tool-augmented agent/system papers and queueing/control study
limitations: Some analyses address tool-rich agents in other domains, but NetOps-specific latency/cost studies are limited in the supplied records
Benefits depend on verifier/tool performance and deployment constraints

excluded_claims: LLMs are proven ready for fully autonomous, unsupervised production NetOps changes without human oversight (no supplied record provides broad, multi-vendor production validation).

There exists a universally accepted, large-scale public benchmark of realistic router/device configurations and annotated operational failures for LLM evaluation (supplied records indicate benchmarking work but not a universally accepted public dataset).

LLMs reliably self-correct arbitrary NetOps mistakes without external deterministic verification signals (evidence suggests self-correction succeeds mainly when reliable external feedback/oracles exist).

Defenses against prompt injection are universally effective across all NetOps-formatted adversarial inputs (supplied defensive studies report strong reductions on their test corpora but not universal effectiveness on NetOps-specific adversarial inputs).
